newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin expects calm Love Parade despite threats.
newsitem.headline: Berlin expects calm Love Parade despite threats.

text.p: Despite neo-Nazi threats, Berlin officials said on Friday they expected Saturday's Love Parade techno music festival -- a street party expecting one million "ravers" -- to be peaceful.

"There were threats against the Love Parade, which we took very seriously," Berlin regional Interior Minister Joerg Schoenbohm told German radio. "Until now police searches have not shown any substance behind the threats.
"But we will stay on the case."

Police on Wednesday raided the homes of 31 suspected right-wing extremists, investigating an anonymous letter Schoenbohm received in June claiming that three anti-tank mines would be laid at the parade if it was not cancelled.

Rightists are hostile to the event, which this year runs under the motto of "Let the Sun Shine in Your Heart", because they say it attracts foreigners to the city and supports music that has "Americanised" German culture.

Police said they also raided homes of about 20 suspected drug dealers on Friday searching for the illegal drug Ecstasy, a stimulant often associated with the techno music scene. A spokesman said officers had confiscated "large" quantities of the substance.

One million techno music fans were expected to dance down a six-km (four-mile) route through central Berlin on Saturday, trailing 40 floats equipped with massive sound systems to supply pulsating beats and synthesiser riffs.
The annual parade, now in its ninth year, has grown since its modest beginnings shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. About 750,000 people came in 1996.

Schoenbohm said his office had received warnings that anarchists planned to move their annual "Chaos Days" riot to Berlin this year to coincide with the Love Parade, which they say is a purely commercial ploy. But he said he did not believe the anarchists posed a danger.
